notes.title: Chapter 3 ETA news, Content Previews, and "State of the Game" address!
notes.content:
Hello Everyone!!!


I hope everyone is doing well, as things seem to be improving on many fronts as of late. Knowing it's been months since my last update, I feel this post is LONG overdue. With so much to cover...let's get right into it! :)


[h1]Chapter 3 Update and ETA for Release[/h1]
I hesitate to title this section so confidently, but I have a few points to state before digging too much into a release date. Namely, I am "reallocating" what parts of the story are in what chapters AND [b][u]taking the game from being 4 chapters to 5 chapters total[/u][/b]. 

I recently had one of my Alpha testers run through the rough draft content for Chapter 3, and I (once again) [i]grossly underestimated[/i] how much content was actually there. What I originally thought was [i]4 hours[/i] turned out to be closer to 6.5-7 hours of content...and I'm at about the halfway marker for my originally-intended story milestones. In short, by the time I'd run through all the story content I originally planned, I would be looking at 14-15 hours for Chapter 3 alone. I ended up making the same decision for Chapter 2, which would have been a similar situation had I not decided to let the story "breathe" by not squeezing it all into Chapter 2. In the long-run, I think it helped a lot with the flow on Chapter 2 and was the right choice. 

[u][b]I came to this decision on Chapter 3 due to the following reasons:[/b][/u]
[i]- The Chapter 2 release was in September of last year, and I'm at mid-way through July with only half the planned story milestones completed[/i]. To finish the story layout I originally planned, I would need another 6-8 months to get the story content down, and that would be with allocating [i]very little[/i] time to "polish and fluff" the game content. It would either be an exorbitant amount of time to complete and/or the content would suffer in quality. I really don't want to make either concession. The game and story naturally "grows", so it's not as if something was missed or "mispaced" during the development cycle, the content comes out at the speed it does regardless of the story layout. 10 hours of content will take the same amount of time regardless of how the story was planned. It's a pain to gauge when developing, which is why I can only know [i]for certain[/i] when someone else playtests the game. 

[i]- There will honestly be [b]plenty[/b] of content for Chapter 3 already. [/i]The 6.5-7 hours thus far doesn't count the remainder of the story content to the new chapter end (which I'm estimating is another 1.5-2 hours). This also doesn't include random encounters, boss fights, and doesn't account for the speed at which people read the dialogue. Some people may also want to replay cinematics or try different branching options for various quests, so it may be even more. I also plan on adding in more things to interact with and do in present areas, so you can expect another 15-30 mins tacked on because of that as well. With all this considered, Chapter 3 will probably come out around 10 hours of content like Chapter 2 did, which seems a pretty reasonable length for a release. 

[i]- Bugs, mistakes, and glitches happen...even with as much preparing and testing is done, one wrong click or typo can tank things pretty hard.[/i] You can almost never spend too much time testing the game for glitches and mistakes, and given the length and complexity of Kedemara, it takes a fair bit of time to go through and test everything before a release. I want to spend more time working in person with my testers (as health conditions in the past made that more difficult) and also focusing on enhancing the current content for Chapter 3...refining the dialogue, adding little touches to spice up the experience, and even adding in more sidequests or fun unlockables and such. 

Time is a very valuable thing!! Please bear in mind, I have friends who will playtest the game for me, but [i][b]all[/b][/i] development is done by me in my own spare time, when not at my full-time job or attending to general life tasks/responsibilities which I manage alone. I try to not "George Lucas" the game too much by making excessive revisions, but sometimes it's necessary to smooth over the rough edges I can't always devote time to improving. The more development time I can focus on making the game as enjoyable as possible, the better. Having the extra time to focus on this will yield a much better end product. Though a labor of love, the game is still labor! :)

With all that said, my target release date for Chapter 3 is going to be [u][b]October 30th 2021[/b][/u], the original release day for Chapter 1. It seems only fitting!!

I find myself retroactively improving older content from time to time, which I believe holds merit as I have been floored at how many people are checking out the game for the first time, thus far. A lot of the streamers I keep in touch with like to play through the previous content before checking out new portions to get themselves up-to-date on any improvements or get a refresher on the story. I like to add in new things for them to uncover or make the process more exciting. 

The biggest change since Chapter 2's release was the Widescreen Mod I made to the game. Instead of a 4:3 aspect ratio (roughly), we're at 16:9 with a resolution of 1280x720. I've yet to hear any complaints and the game seems to run roughly the same as before. The daunting task that still hangs over me is reformatting the text for a widescreen-sized text box. When expanding the playable screen area in the game, you also get more room for text in the dialogue boxes. This is good and bad, since I can space text out visually, making it easier to read...but will now have ~15 hours of text content to go and fix (and another 1 or 2 hours of early Chapter 3). This is going to be a work-in-progress task for some time. All the text is visible as-is, it's just not as pretty. My method is going to be reformatting major dialogue interactions and cutscenes first, then moving on to main character dialogue before reformatting all the smaller encounters with NPCs and objects. Your patience and understanding is appreciated...it is quite the undertaking, but will be worth it in the end. 

Besides this, the other major news will be the expansion from 4 total chapters to 5 total for the game. I'll be noting this change on the Steam store page, but felt it bore repeating as some people may be confused at the end of Chapter 4 wondering why the game didn't conclude yet. 

[b][h2]What to Expect Regarding Chapter 4[/h2][/b]
There is still some FANTASTIC content that is yet to be completed for Chapter 3, so don't be dismayed...some of the best is being saved for last. In regards to Chapter 4, we'll see the world "expanding" yet again, as we did in Chapter 2 and in Chapter 3. You'll see more open exploration and movement around the world on a large scale in Chapter 4, as well as an increase in city size. You run into a huge capital city in Chapter 3, but you will encounter at least 2 or 3 more in Chapter 4. These are multi-map cities (have to do a screen transition to access different areas) that should be thick with environment and ambience. 

This was another reason why I feel cutting Chapter 3 where I will is the right decision. There is a great deal of mapping yet to be done and that also takes a lot of time. I am not particularly great at this aspect of game design, but I do want to put as much in as I can. The cities in Chapter 4 should be VERY distinct in their tilesets and themes, making for a good change of pace while being thematically-consistent given their locations in the world. 

While we have a new member joining Deirdre's crew in Chapter 3, there will be no new additions past that. A party of 7 should be plenty and adding another permanent team member adds exponential difficulty to balance. You will see some friends temporarily joining for certain quests or events, so that should be a fun addition when we get there!



My apologies on the wordy update, though there was a lot to cover. I've reached out to testers, friends, and streamers about the Chapter 3 release and they are excited to experience it in full. There's never a dull moment in the company of Deirdre and her friends, so expect nothing less as you embark with them once again. I should hope that this chapter in their journey proves even more engaging than the previous two, and I believe it will. I appreciate the support from all of you as you play the game, monitor its progress, stream its content, and send your messages of encouragement and enjoyment! I wish you all well and look forward to sharing the next part of Deirdre's story with you! :)

notes.title: New Features and Ch. 3 Progress Update!
notes.content:
[h1]Hello everyone! [/h1]

It's hard to believe it's been nearly 6 months since the Chapter 2 release, but here we are! I've been thrilled to see people's reactions and wonderfully kind words concerning the game recently, I can always see room for improvement in the game, but it's reassuring to know that people are still enjoying the new content regardless. I am [b]floored[/b] at the amount of people who have played the game so far! A [b][u]BIG[/u][/b] thank you to everyone who has played, streamed, shared with friends, and reached out to me about the game. It's your encouragement and support that helps me push myself to keep improving the game and press onward as we all share in Deirdre's journey together! 

There's plenty to discuss, so let's get cracking!! :)

[h2][b]
"Expanding Horizons"[/b][/h2]
This is something I've admittedly been ignoring for a while, but I've gotten this question numerous times from players...."Why isn't the game in 16:9 (widescreen)?" I stuck to this decision for two reasons:

[i]- My aesthetic rationale was that the 4:3 aspect ratio made the game feel more like an older RPG, appropriate to the SNES/Genesis era. While in principal that's true, most of us aren't playing on 4:3 monitors or CRTs. With the rise of retro games found on various platforms, it could be argued this isn't a big deal...but I doubt I'd receive complaints that the game ISN'T in 4:3 from many players.
- The game will not scroll/run as smoothly, was my other reasoning. RPG Maker creates games in a very oddball resolution of 816x624, plugins have to be used to manipulate this. Kedemara currently runs in 941x720, the way to get a vertical resolution of 720p while maintaining the same aspect ratio/proportions. While framerates always game back great on a variety of systems, when bumping this up to a more standard 1280x720 resolution, I saw the game ran basically the same. There will always be some stutter with scrolling since the nature of Javascript and the engine may cause this. Tl;dr = I wanted the game to run smoother, but in 1280x720 it runs just as well. [/i]

[b]
From here forward, I'll be designing Chapter 3 to run in a widescreen aspect ratio. By the next patch I release, Chapters 1+2 [i]WILL have this applied[/i], which will be before Chapter 3 is finished or released. A few sidenotes to keep in mind on the shift for Chapters 1 and 2:[/b]

[i]- This will only affect the viewable area of the game, so graphical assets like tiles, sprites, and animations should be largely unaffected. The placement of some enemies in combat will need adjusting, but that is very quick and easy to fix. On the whole, you'll just see more of the map. If that particular map is smaller than 1280x720 you'll still see a black area, this is just how the game handles "blank space", but for larger areas you'll notice a big difference...Amie pun slightly intended ;-)
- When you change resolutions or use various formatting "tags", Word Wrap can do some funky things in RPG Maker text boxes...so spacing and such is all done manually when I make them. Because of this, a great majority of the dialogue text in Chapters 1+2 (and the earlier part of Chapter 3) will have dialogue text that is very left-aligned. It will all be visible, but there will be some extra space to the right as increasing the game's resolution also increases the text space in dialogue boxes. 
- Changing this will be a methodical process, but I'll start with title screens, center-aligned text announcements, and cutscene dialogue that is more straightforward without branching options. With how much time I'll need to be sinking into Chapter 3's development...it may be some time before I can get 100% of the text filled-out for 16:9 text boxes. Just know it probably bothers me far more than it bothers any of you lol.[/i]

I have one of my trusted Alpha-testers scouring through the game for events/cutscenes that would be obviously affected by this change. I can think of a few but wanted to have someone check for anything I may have forgotten. These will take precedence as "popouts" and such can be a little jarring to the player. I won't push it out until it has been combed-through adequately. All in all, she's told me it's quite enjoyable playing in the new widescreen layout and feels the change is worthwhile. I hope all of you like the change as well!


[h2][b]Chapter 3 News[/b][/h2]
In these past 6 months, I can honestly say things haven't been smooth sailing in regards to everyday life and local circumstances for me. I always say it, but I'm not as far along as I'd like for this current chapter. However, just like with Ch.2, I didn't realize how much content I already had. My main Alpha-tester has run through what I have for Chapter 3 so far and I'm sitting at [b]about 3-3.5 hours so far.[/b] Not great, but I'm going to be pushing myself harder to get progress sped up. 

[i]- The cities are going to be MUCH larger in this Chapter, so a place like Clachandun will be more common to see than Corning. Some of these cities will span several maps that you'll transition between, so the scale is much more grand in this chapter. 
- There will be some flexibility in how you experience the story later in the Chapter, essentially you won't HAVE to do some of the story in a set order, but this will introduce the overworld map and a few other things I'd like to see happen in this chapter.
- ANOTHER new character will be joining your party in Chapter 3! I've run this character by a few of my Testers and friends, and she's been a big hit thus far. Definitely larger than life, with plenty of personality to spare, I hope you'll grow to love her just as much as the rest of Deirdre's friends!
- Cutscenes! Cutscenes everywhere!! I can get a little trigger-happy with cutscenes, but I am working on getting a better balance between large text-only conversations and describing past events and such with "cutscenes". The large amounts of text can get tiring, so finding the right groove for both is something I'm still working on. When I have some more content completed, I'll eventually be posting a teaser trailer for Chapter 3 to show some of the progress. I'm very happy with how things are transpiring, I certainly hope everyone else will be too! [/i]



Sorry for the super long, WAY overdue post! I'm very excited to show everyone what is in store for Chapter 3, and I hope you guys are excited to experience it as well!
- Andrew (Creator)

I refuse to "name any names" on who made it, but a 3rd party plugin creator is who made the paid Steam Achievements script used in my game. I had every.single.one working except for the two mentioned in my previous patch update ("Buccaneer Buster" and "Unfortunate Telling"). When I looked at the plugin commands for both, I saw that part of it was capitalized and that "Achievement" was spelled "Achivement" as well, so I made everything lower case and fixed the typo assuming that was the problem.

Well, here we are again today and it's STILL not working for everyone! I spent 30 mins going back and forth trying to figure out what the problem was, until I realized all my other achievements just had the script command copied from the ReadMe file and [i]I never once noticed the spelling...[/i] The plugin was coded so that the word "Achievement" was supposed to be (incorrectly) spelled "A-C-H-I-V-E-M-E-N-T" in order for it to work. So I spelled it wrong when typing in the plugin command and sure enough, that fixed the problem ːsteamfacepalmː

There is ABOUT 20-30 mins of content already in a "playable state", which just tells me this chapter may end up even bigger than Chapter 2 was. It's difficult to gauge the scope at this time, as I know the major story arc(s) already, but when a good idea pops into my head for a scene or interaction, I don't want it to go to waste...so the story can swell quite a bit over time. I'm focusing a great deal on fleshing out the previously presented lore, expanding on the history/experiences of characters you heard of from the distant past, and improving on the cutscenes and dramatic interludes in the story. All in all, I hope Chapter 3 can improve on what I presented in Chapters 1 and 2, making the story that much more enjoyable for everyone. I can't wait to show everyone what Chapter 3 has in store! (but it may be a while...lol)


Hopefully everyone got a little chuckle out of the Steam Achievements fiasco and enjoys some of the updates, but everything should be 100% now and I'll get back to work on Chapter 3! Thank you to those who let me know and I hope everyone is enjoying the game so far!

notes.title: Chapter 2 is now LIVE!
notes.content:
[h3]Hello all!

Through many trials and setbacks, that I'm sure we've all had our fair share of this year, [u][b]Chapter 2 of the game is NOW live![/b][/u]

As promised, I have [i]throughly[/i] playtested this deployment package myself to check for any major bugs. Though some of the minor text formatting and other small oversights will be resolved by me when I can devote more time. I think everyone will be pleasantly surprised at how much content is available with Chapter 2, I certainly hope you find it enjoyable to experience as well! I'll keep this succinct as I'm still ironing out some of the marketing materials (screenshots, trailers, etc.) for this release today. Here are a few notes and points I want to make everyone savvy to...[/h3]

[h1]Chapter 1:[/h1]
- As hinted at above, I have played through this portion and have made some fixes on issues that came up with this deployment package. Most of these were related to some "trimming" I did with the Ch. 2 deployment package, but if you experienced issues with a prior deployment, the game should have these issues resolved.
- More "polish" has been applied to Chapter 1 overall...from text formatting, unifying some of the lore text/backstory, and even adding animations with new sprites are among some of the changes made. As noted in a previous Steam announcement, much of the music has been changed around as well...especially for your companion's themes. 
- If you've not played Chapter 1 in the past few months, I would strongly recommend giving it a go again. Given the complexity of Chapter 2's story content, and how much it elaborates on more subtle historical lore mentioned in Chapter 1, I have made certain concepts or information a bit more amplified to assist in unifying these narrative points. Being familiar with the lore in general will assist a great deal with understanding the story elements found in Chapter 2. I also feel the quality of the dialogue has improved some as well. 
- If there are functionality issues with save games, this can unfortunately be due to some past fixes that needed applying. When in doubt, it's better to start fresh. It'll be great to see the new changes anyways!

[b]**EDIT (9-3-2020)**[/b]
I have been able to devote some time to a few of the "polish" updates that I've wanted to add in for Chapter 1 thus far...these are including, but not limited to:
- Longdale Warehouse scene has been streamlined to not have jarring "jump cuts" between the events. This required streamlining the eventing (which was early on and poorly organized), but it flows much better now
- Picked a more appropriate sprite for the Sewer boss
- Fixed/re-worked dialogue bits that had characters missing on the map screen, though they were speaking in dialogue boxes. (one or two more scenes to go)
- Expanded cutscene in the later part of the ship scene, adding better effect transitions and effects to the scene.
- Added a more fitting introduction scene to the encampment, explaining the setting. Guards were also given "guidance dialogue" to help progress through that area effectively. 
- Final cutscene has received some tweaks to make it look smoother. 

[h1]Chapter 2:[/h1]
- Chapter 2 is big...VERY big. It's hard to gauge it with pinpoint accuracy, since many people read or explore at a different pace, but the estimate from playtesters and my own playthrough is that Chapter 2 is about 9 - 10 hours on it's own, if you encounter all the narrative and flavor content. Given the previous estimates of Chapter 1 being roughly 5+ hours, we'd be looking at nearly 15 hours of content to run through everything. Again, this can vary from person to person, and most people will discover new things with each playthrough. If the large chunk of Steam achievements didn't imply it clearly enough, there is a LOT to discover! :)
- Much like Chapter 1, the game doesn't [i]force[/i] you to experience all the side content if you don't wish to. However, with the story being the focus of the game (and what the most time is invested in), it won't be the experience I'd like you to have. I do make the game this way since some people have already played through certain parts and may not want to go through everything [i]again[/i]...but it does pay to explore! You never know what you'll find this time around!

- The spirit and "feel" of the game and characters is certainly alive and present in this chapter of the game, but as characters develop and Deirdre becomes more acquainted with the world at large and its inhabitants, things may not always be sunshine and roses for Deirdre and her companions. More dramatic elements are to be found in this chapter than in Chapter 1, but the whimsical nature and comedic heart of the story is still very alive and present in Chapter 2. Despite whatever may transpire, hope remains for those who seek it :)



I certainly hope everyone enjoys the game and looks forward to this and future chapters in Deirdre's story! Yes, I will begin working on Chapter 3 very shortly!
- Andrew (Creator)

It took a day or two, but I've changed the maps in Raynewood Outskirts and Raynewood Forest to no longer have that particular tile. It is replaced by a more realistic tree graphic that I must admit looks better. A few other aesthetic tweaks were made to Raynewood Forest as well, but I feel they improve it enough to justify the time and effort. 

-Armor items readjustment-
In the spirit of keeping the game simple, I felt the Head, Chest, Offhand, and Accessories slots became a little overwhelming from a stat balancing and player perspective. From now on [i]*chest item upgrades will coincide with an actor's change of outfit/sprite* [/i](i.e. - When Deirdre's sprite model changes, so will her chest armor). Since RPG Maker doesn't really display head, offhand, or accessory changes it seems fine to leave those as-is. [u][b]Any save games pre-Kassian Encampment should experience NO issues with this aspect of the update[/b][/u]. Since it's only affecting Chest armor and that is so late in the game that new ones are available, I don't believe it will cause any real problems. All of the tests even with other armor seemed to experience no issues with crashing. If you do experience a problem, please let me know so I can resolve it. 

[h2]
**CHAPTER 2 NEWS**
[/h2]
Chapter 2 is still plugging away to completion, but I will add a small bit of information. Given the current situation regarding the international pandemic, I will have to move from my current residence soon. I do not like to make excuses nor do I really like to bring my personal affairs into such spaces, but I felt it was fair to explain why there will be some hold-up. Since many different factors are at play, it will be difficult for me to give a good ETA right now. Without a doubt, t[u][b]here will be a Chapter 2 release this year.[/b][/u] While it will be well-tested for bugs, Chapter 2 may start off a bit more content-sparse than I would like upon its release. I always view the game as a living being that can always improve and be better refined. Steam is a platform that allows that, and I strive to continually adjust and improve the game for everyone when I can. While the main core of the story will be solid and present, some of the finer details like side-events, big conversation option lists, and interactive environments may be a bit lacking with the initial release. Nonetheless, the core story will be there and impactful. I am looking forward to everyone's thoughts on it! :)


I'd like to thank you all for your support. It shows in the metrics numbers I receive from Steam. I am pleasantly surprised to see so many folks enjoying the game, and I hope to keep improving as we all experience Deirdre's story together! :)


- Andrew (Creator)

notes.title: Chapter 2 Progress Update!
notes.content:
[h3][i]Hello all!

I hope everyone is taking appropriate measures to be safe and is in good health. I wanted to take this opportunity to give some more detailed info about the next Chapter of Kedemara, set for release sometime this year! Given the difficulties we've all experienced from the recent pandemic, and a few other life complications I've personally experienced over the last 6 months, progress on Chapter 2 has proven a bit more time consuming than I originally anticipated, but I have some excellent news that should make the wait quite worth the time it has taken thus far! The following bullet points will give summaries of milestones already reached (with details below them), another section detailing what's in the works, and some exciting bits to explain what to expect in Chapter 2. I will also make a few feature announcements regarding Chapter 3:[/i][/h3]
[h2][u][b]
**COMPLETED**[/b][/u][/h2]
[b]- Major story arcs for Chapter 2 are all accounted for[/b]
Though I have the main thread of the story for the entire game already planned/written, I like to pop in some smaller ones per-chapter and some more details here and there as I go. The scale of Deirdre's journey, and the world she is venturing into, will definitely increase in size with Chapter 2. I am looking forward to everyone learning more about her companions and some of the new friends they make along the way. 

[b]- All mapping for the game's levels will be completed by tonight[/b]
The size of maps in the first half is about on-par with what you'd see in Chapter 1. The part I am currently working on has several maps that are MUCH larger in comparison. One of the cities you visit is close to 3.5-4 times the size of Port Brahma. I don't want to spoil anything, but I will say many of the locales are quite unique and fun, while still fitting the general theme of the game. 
[b]
- The first "half" of the story has already been beta tested[/b]
I submitted the first half of Chapter 2 to my beta testers and that portion is in a very playable state, arguably already "completed". A few bugs were found in the process, but overall it came out quite well. Everyone has loved the story and direction thus far, along with some of the new NPCs and party characters that were introduced. More on this later...

[b]- Two new characters already designed/created in the game.[/b]
Not as glamorous of an update, but with the level of character development I try to put in the party members, it can take some time to tweak both their combat and character details to make sure they suit the party well. So far the beta testers have loved the new additions in and out of combat, bringing even more balance and variety to Deirdre's companions. 

[h2][u][b]
**IN PROGRESS**[/b][/u][/h2]
[b]- Coding/Eventing 2nd half of the Chapter.[/b]
As stated above, we have an arguably completed first half of Chapter 2 already done, so that just leaves the 2nd half of course. Given the progress made on the Chapter 2 so far, I feel the time and effort put into it will be well worth the wait. I again, have a neat detail which will be mentioned farther down.
[b]
- Selecting the remainder of the music tracks.[/b]
The first half features a great track made by my colleague Austin, I feel it suits the area of the game perfectly and is intensely catchy. Hopefully we can hear more from him, but with recent developments in the world in general, it has been trying for him to create some new tracks. While Chapter 1 has undergone some switches to the music, I feel the 2nd half should hit just as hard if not more than the first. 

[b]- Adjustments on combat stats/items.[/b]
I typically leave this for the end to see what the appropriate level and challenge for players would be. I HATE a game that forces grinding to get characters to appropriate levels, so the game should be fine going from point a to point b, or if you'd like a leg up on the competition, you can spend some time grinding random encounter areas. I try to pay a lot of attention to this as it can become frustrating for newcomers and veterans alike. 

[h2][b]The Beta Test Results:[/b][/h2]
One of the big surprises I had about Chapter 2 after my beta testers gave their results, was how big it was so far. When I polled them asking how much playtime they had, the average came out to 6 HOURS! [u][b]Yes, the first half of Chapter 2 alone has 6 hours of content![/b][/u] Even I was surprised, as I've been lucky to have time to work on the game, much less do a full run-through. [b]This would put my estimate for Chapter 2's length at about 11-12 hours of content in total[/b]. Combined with Chapter 1, that's roughly 17 hours of content. A few of them said that Chapter 2 would be fine to end there, but I believe in giving people their money's worth (lol) so I'm going to push myself to maintain the current quality standards and deliver the full story arc I was planning for everyone. I certainly hope everyone feels the same as they did, that the wait is worth it for the final product.


[h2][b]WHAT TO LOOK FORWARD TO IN CHAPTER 3!![/b][/h2]
- I believe in taking the "soft introduction" route when it comes to game mechanics, starting off with very simple implementations of a concept or challenge and then gradually increasing the difficulty in following areas. There will be much more of that in Chapter 2, but Chapter 3 will be where much of this comes to fruition and begins asking more of the player in terms of puzzle solving and other various concepts I'm working into the game. Expect some of the concepts introduced in Chapter 2 to be present in Chapter 3!

- More "quests" will be available in Chapter 3, there are a couple that are introduced in Chapter 2, but it is not a major part of the game at that point. In Chapter 3, these quests will often result in either sizeable monetary rewards or very unique/powerful items only acquirable in that manner. Since some of these will be of task-oriented nature they will be completely voluntary and not required to progress in the game. Some minor story elements may be revealed or accessible by these means, but it should not hinder the main story in any way by skipping. 

- Overworld exploration will introduced in Chapter 3 (finally, I know lol), but I have had a few reasons to hold off until then. The first being that you're going almost everywhere on foot, so simply walking across a large continent reduces the sense of scale you have for Aetheria...something I'd like to avoid. I have to withhold story spoilers, but lets just say there is little point to traversing backwards at this point in the story. Overworld exploration will make much more sense in regards to the story during Chapter 3, you will also have more means to travel quickly so the sense of scale should feel maintained by then.  

- Character outfit changes will also be happening in Chapter 3 for all your party members . Again, I feel this change makes a great deal more sense at this time in the story, it will also seem more rewarding when the change has meaning behind it. I am currently waffling on whether or not to have a wardrobe change for one of the characters at the end of Chapter 2, but we'll just have to wait and see where it heads. Oh, and yes, Tessa will [i]finally [/i]learn where Marsha got her hat from ;-)



[i]Well, I want to thank everyone for their support and patience with me thus far. It is honestly a joy to work on this and hearing from players about their enjoyment of the game makes me so happy. Hearkening back to my D&D days as a Dungeon Master, happy players make me a happy DM....so happy gamers make me a happy dev. I certainly hope experiencing Deirdre's story remains something I can continue enjoying with you guys for many days to come. Thank you all so very much! :)


- Andrew (Creator)[/i]

notes.title: Kedemara Ch.1 Content Update! (Version 1.1)
notes.content:
Hello everyone!!

Thank you all so much for your interest in Kedemara! It's been a bumpy road getting where we are now, but to me it's worth [i]every second of work[/i] to see this come to fruition.  I couldn't do it without the encouragement and support of my colleagues Austin and Emily. A special thanks to our dedicated playtesters as well! Thanks to Aaron, Jorge, Ross, Jose, Joshua, and Levi for all the time they spent helping us refine the game and pushing us to constantly improve. [b]Couldn't have done it without all of you![/b] 

[b]Last but not least[/b], thank you to [b]EVERY single person[/b] who has played this game despite not knowing me from Adam. There's no shortage of other things to do in the world, but you all took a chance on my game and I am thrilled to hear people enjoying and having fun playing the game! It's wonderful to share Deirdre's story with all of you and I hope you continue to grow fond of her, along with her companions, as the rest of her story unfolds! 


Without further ado, let's get to the update notes!

[h1][b]Chapter 1 Updates[/b][/h1]

[h2][b]-NEW Content Additions-[/b][/h2]
There has been a considerable amount of content added to Longdale (first town in the game), as it's early on and felt a bit sparse compared to later places in the game given its size. Here are a few additions broken down by area...

[b](Longdale)[/b]
[i]- [u]5 brand new, accessible buildings have been added to the town[/u] (Inn, Stable, Shop, Smithy, Teahouse) along with the Northeast corner of town no longer being blocked-off by town guards. The new buildings are all [b]packed [/b]with NPCs and/or items to interact with. Some NPCs previously found in town have been moved into these buildings as well. This will offer more information about Deirdre's years in town and show the relationships she built with fellow townspeople. 
- A "Secret Building" has been added with a hidden entrance in Longdale! A rare item lay somewhere inside this building...but don't tell just anyone when you find it! [b]"It's a secret to EVERYONE"!![/b]
- For those who have progressed past Longdale already, you'll find a new person is hanging out in the tavern...though he'll look familiar to you! Go talk to him when you see him![/i]
[b]
(Raynewood)[/b]
[i]- In Fanum Sylvis (the Cathedral in Raynewood), Amie has been given considerably more conversation content in the Minister's Quarters upstairs. After reading the book on The Arbiter and the Wicked King, Amie will appear and you have multiple topics you can discuss with her. This should give a bit more insight to her past as a character, something that felt lacking in the previous versions of the game. [/i]

[b](??????)[/b]
[i]- There is currently a SECOND secret room hidden in Ch1 of the game as well! [u]As a hint, the entrance to this secret room is in a place with sand![/u][/i]


[h2][b]-Content Changes-[/b][/h2][i]
- Longdale theme has been changed to something more suiting its new environment and feel. 
- Some layout changes were made to the Orphanage, now Deirdre and Granny Moira's sprites should be visible during their conversation and not blocked by the text banners. 
- Tova no longer randomly blocks the way to Granny Moira...but she'll still need hugs before you go!
- It is now completely IMPOSSIBLE to die in the battle tutorial with Will (don't ask, it's a long story). 
- Changed the interaction animations when you first meet Amie. These have bothered me since the release and now they should be much better. 
- Fixed various bugs and some timing issues with encounters or sprite movements. [/i]


"So what about Chapter 2?" You ask?... ːsteamhappyː

[b][h1]**CHAPTER 2 NEWS**[/h1][/b]

[i]While I don't have a solid ETA for release, I can tell you right now that our playtesters are LOVING it thus far. I'm hoping to beef Chapter 1 up some (as this update shows), but Chapter 2 is just fantastic in my opinion and will be well worth the wait. [/i]

[h2][u][b]Here's a few things to expect concerning Chapter 2![/b][/u][/h2]
[i]- This chapter is going to be MASSIVE. I am roughly 1/2 of the way through the planned story content and it's already at 3-4 hours of content. If I had to estimate, we're looking at a 6-7 hour long chapter. We will definitely be at least 10+ hours including Chapter 1's content. 
- There is confirmed [b][u]TWO NEW CHARACTERS[/u][/b] who will be joining your party. (Don't worry, Harold's not one of them). So far the playtesters love the characters and  feel they are perfect additions to Deirdre's companions. 
- [u][b]Ultimas[/b][/u] ARE coming in Chapter 2!! I already have them ready to roll, you'll acquire your first ones in the earlier part of Chapter 2. Expect more to come later in the chapter!
- New "puzzle" (using that word loosely) mechanics will be introduced in dungeons and some towns. They will start with very simple "introductions" to the concepts, then get blended in for more challenging content later in the game. 
- Austin has been trying his hand at composing and will be working more of his compositions into the game music. Keep an eye (or ear) out for the Ch2 trailer to hear a sneak peek of some![/i]


On a sidenote, I want to make something [u]brutally clear[/u]...[b]Chapter 2 is ALSO going to be FREE[/b]. Non-team members have, with good intentions, implored that I start charging by Chapter 2. While I entertained the idea for a while, I honestly want to keep Kedemara free as long as I possibly can. I [u]do not [/u]develop this game full-time, it's done in my free time, so it's not a source of income for me currently. I would rather as many people as possible get to play the game as opposed to just trying to make a buck. If a time comes where help will be needed to make the game develop further, we'll let you guys know. 

In the meantime, please keep enjoying the game!

- Andrew (Creator)
